subject: Slate v2 onboarding: integration & governance check
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Slate AI <integration@slate.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Slate v2 onboarding: integration & governance check

Hi team,

Slate (integration@slate.ai) just shared a candidate: Slate v2 (open checkpoints + new tokenizer). They want to go live for a pilot with Acme Payments next month. Before we sign off I need a quick cross-functional read on integration risk and whether we need to hard-pin the existing variant for safety. High-level asks: 

- Infra: what compatibility gaps (tokenizer, layer names, KV cache layout) do we expect from a drop-in load?
- Product: rollout constraints — metrics that would force a rollback or pin (latency, cost, hallucination rate, token-change regressions).
- Reliability: what can we run in staging/canary to catch subtle regressions?

Attachments: slate_v2-release-notes.pdf (vendor release notes).

Goal: decide on a gating policy by EOD Friday so Sales can confirm pilot window. If you need artifacts from Slate (tokenizer vocab, sample checkpoint, smoke tests), call them out.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Slate AI <integration@slate.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Slate v2 onboarding: integration & governance check

Kimberly — thanks for the flag. Quick initial notes from infra perspective: 

- Tokenizer: vendor notes say a modified BPE with ~3k token delta vs our canonical tokenizer. That usually causes embedding drift and token-count changes that affect latency/cost. We need the tokenizer files and a mapping so we can run tokenization parity tests.
- KV/cache layout: early glance looks compatible, but fused-op naming differs (we'll need a non-destructive adapter for the checkpoint loader).
- Model names & shapes: request the actual checkpoint metadata; sometimes hidden singleton dims break our kernel selection path.

Suggested plan (timeline ~2 weeks):
1) Vendor artifact intake: tokenizer vocab, sample checkpoint, config.json, and a 1000-prompt smoke set (privacy-safe).
2) Staging run: smoke + perf baseline vs current variant (1 day run).
3) Canary: 5% traffic with toggle and automatic rollback on latency > 2x P50 or token rate deviation > 15%.

Pin recommendation: do NOT hard-pin globally pre-emptively. Instead create a soft-pin strategy: pin the default route to current stable variant, enable Slate v2 behind a toggle with auto-fallback. If staging shows model-level incompatibilities we follow emergency pin.

I'll formalize a detailed compatibility checklist if everyone agrees.

—Karthik
Head of Serving Infrastructure
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Slate v2 onboarding: integration & governance check

Agree with Karthik's plan — a couple product-level constraints to lock in: 

- Success metrics for this pilot (must be agreed before canary): P50 latency delta <= +20ms, token-cost change <= +10%, hallucination/noise as measured by our eval harness not greater than current variant by more than 5% on our prompt set.
- Rollout phases: internal QA -> limited pilot (Acme Payments) -> gradual expansion. No GA announcement until pilot completes.
- Fallback mapping: we need a deterministic fallback mapping for any new tool-calls or function-calling changes (if the model changes function output shapes/formats).

Please add a column to the checklist for product gate verification and link the signals to our rollout doc (I've added a stub). Also Sales needs a short blurb they can share with the pilot customer explaining the toggle/backout plan.

Attachment: product-rollout-checklist.md (checklist template).

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Slate AI <integration@slate.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Slate v2 onboarding: integration & governance check

Thanks — helpful notes. Summarizing agreed next steps and owners: 

- Slate AI to provide artifacts: tokenizer files, sample checkpoint, config.json, and a 1k prompt smoke set (owner: Slate, requested by EOD Wed).
- Infra (Karthik + Marcus): produce compatibility checklist and run staging smoke tests (ETA: 5 business days after artifacts). Will attach integration-checklist.csv and slate_v2-smoke-report.pdf to the ticket.
- Product (Laura): finalize acceptance thresholds and provide the Sales blurb for the pilot.
- Ops (Dev): prepare toggle + auto-fallback policy and verify observability hooks (per-token cost, hallucination signal).

Decision on pinning: as discussed, we will NOT hard-pin by default. Implement soft-pin/toggle for canary and reserve the right to hard-pin if staging/canary metrics breach agreed thresholds.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_slate-onboard-plan, Jira INFRA-3421.

I can sync 20m tomorrow if anyone wants a live alignment before we request artifacts.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
